title: MCU Surprise: ‘VisionQuest’ Finale Teases the Return of [SPOILER] in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’
description:
SPOILER WARNING: This story contains major spoilers for “Forever,” the finale episode of “VisionQuest,” now streaming on Disney+.

	The WandaVision
body:
SPOILER WARNING: This story contains major spoilers for “Forever,” the finale episode of “VisionQuest,” now streaming on Disney+.

	The WandaVision Saga has come to a close with the final hour of the Disney+ series “VisionQuest.” But it seems as though the story of the ultrapowerful Scarlet Witch, the synthezoid Vision and their superpowered children will continue in the MCU.

	The finale episode sees Paul Bettany’s Vision reunite with his and Wanda Maximoff’s (Elizabeth Olsen) grown-up sons, Ruaridh Mollica’s Tommy Maximoff (who was key to the series) and Joe Locke’s Billy Maximoff (whose eleventh-hour arrival completes the family reunion). Then, the post-credit scene replays the end of 2022’s feature film “Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness,” where Wanda eradicated the Darkhold from all of the multiverse before (seemingly) being crushed from within a mountain.
	



	

									Getty Images for BFI
	



	However, this time, the scene continues with the appearance of Robert Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom, who lifts the rubble off Wanda and addresses her. 

	“Scarlett Witch, awaken — your power will be mine,” Doom says, as Wanda gasps and opens her eyes. 

	The coda confirms fan speculation that Olsen’s Wanda would return as the Avengers face off against Doom in future Marvel projects, which could include “Avengers: Doomsday,” out Dec. 18. 

	Olsen first appeared as Wanda in the post-credits scene for 2014’s “Captain America: The Winter Soldier,” which set up her full-fledged debut in 2015’s “Avengers: Age of Ultron.” Despite her wide-ranging powers of telekinesis and mind manipulation, Wanda’s first forays in the MCU were laden with tragedy, including the death of her brother Pietro (Aaron Taylor-Johnson), the devastation of her home country of Sokovia in “Age of Ultron,” and then the death of her beloved Vision (Paul Bettany) in 2018’s “Avengers: Infinity War.”
	

	That trauma led to 2021’s “WandaVision,” Marvel Studios‘ first TV series for Disney+, in which Wanda’s overwhelming grief led her to take over an entire New Jersey town and transform it into a recreation of American sitcoms — complete with a reconstituted Vision and two twin sons, Billy and Tommy. By the end of the series, she had to let go of Vision and her sons, all while her interactions with the witch Agatha Harkness (Kathryn Hahn) revealed Wanda to be the Scarlet Witch, one of the most powerful beings in the Marvel universe. Agatha’s witchy, post-“WandaVision” escapades continued in the 2024 Disney+ series “Agatha All Along,” which introduced Joe Locke as Wanda and Vision’s grown-up son Billy Maximoff. 

	Wanda’s story continued in 2022’s feature film “Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness,” in which her grief from the loss of her children led her to turn fully evil as the film’s central villain. She brutally killed anyone standing in opposition to her desire to find her boys within the multiverse, fueled by the corrupting book of magic, the Darkhold. By the end, Wanda understood all the harm she had caused, and she eradicated the Darkhold from all of the multiverse before (seemingly) being crushed from within Wundagore mountain.

	When asked by Variety in 2022 whether she hoped to play Wanda again, however, Olsen sounded optimistic.

	“It’s weird that I’m expecting to return, but no one’s told me I’m doing anything!” she said with a laugh. “But in my mind, I’m just making the assumption that they’ll have me again. I don’t know to what capacity, but I hope I’m back. I hope there’s also more fun to be had in something different.”

schema.headline: MCU Surprise: ‘VisionQuest’ Finale Teases the Return of [SPOILER] in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’

title: Brandy and Monica Announce ‘The Boy Is Mine’ 2027 Residency at Las Vegas’ Resorts World
description:
Brandy and Monica have announced “The Boy Is Mine Vegas Residency,” their first-ever series of shows in Las Vegas.

	The R&B icons announced the re
body:
Brandy and Monica have announced “The Boy Is Mine Vegas Residency,” their first-ever series of shows in Las Vegas.

	The R&B icons announced the residency following a performance of their collaborative hit “The Boy Is Mine” on “Dancing With the Stars” during its Grammy-themed episode on Tuesday night. The 10-date residency will take place at Resorts World Las Vegas, kicking off on May 29 with performances through June before concluding on July 17.
	

	Produced by the Black Promoters Collective, the residency comes following their sold-out “The Boy Is Mine” tour, which saw each artist trading off to perform hits and deep cuts from their respective catalogs. Following the conclusion of the tour in December 2025, Brandy and Monica continued to perform together at the St. Lucia Jazz & Arts Festival and a co-headlining performance at the 2026 Essence Festival of Culture. Read Variety‘s review of Brandy and Monica’s Los Angeles tour stop here.

	In a statement shared with Variety, Monica says that she did not initially envision the tour extending to a residency. “Originally, it was planned as a one and done, but I’ll be honest, after the first night, I realized it was far deeper,” she said, touching on the key to her working relationship with Brandy. “I think the most important factor in any relationship or friendship, especially one that has a partnership like ours, is communication. Communication is key, and keeping other people out, allowing us to speak about the things that matter, to talk about things when one may like something or may not like something, making sure other people’s feelings don’t become our own. [It’s] the key component to how we make sure things work best.”
	

	“BPC is proud to be working with Brandy and Monica again,” says Shelby Joyner, President of Black Promoters Collective, in a statement. “We saw on The Boy Is Mine tour how much it meant to fans to see them share a stage, and I’m excited to build on what we created together. Bringing The Boy Is Mine to Las Vegas as Black Promoters Collective’s first residency is a big moment for us. We’ve built BPC by betting on artists we believe in and listening to their fans. This residency takes that work into a new arena for our company, and I can’t think of two artists I’d rather take that step with.”

	American Express presale begins on November 11 at 10 a.m. PT, followed by artist presale at 12 p.m. PT. Local presales start on November 12 at 10 a.m. PT, and general onsale kicks off on November 20 at 10 a.m. PT.

	Check out “The Boy Is Mine Vegas Residency” dates below:

	Saturday, May 29 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasSunday, May 30 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasWednesday, June 2 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasFriday, June 4 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasSaturday, June 5 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasFriday, July 9 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasSaturday, July 10 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasWednesday, July 14 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasFriday, July 16 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las VegasSaturday, July 17 – Las Vegas, NV @ Resorts World Las Vegas



	

	



	With additional reporting from Tim Chan

title: Brenda Song Says She Was ‘Overworked’ and ‘Underpaid’ on ‘The Suite Life of Zack and Cody,’ Recalls Fainting on Set: I Thought, ‘Am I Having a Panic Attack?’
description: Brenda Song recently revealed that she felt she was “overworked” and “underpaid” while starring on “The Suite Life of Zack and Cody.” The “Running
body:
Brenda Song recently revealed that she felt she was “overworked” and “underpaid” while starring on “The Suite Life of Zack and Cody.” The “Running Point” actress opened up about her experience working on the Disney Channel sitcom while appearing on her former co-star Dylan Sprouse’s and co-host Brendan Columbus’ “Wildmen” podcast.

	“I’ve been curious to ask you about this. Like, I feel like there are parts of the ‘Suite Life’ that are, like, black holes for me. Like, I don’t remember years of my life,” Song said, before moving onto the subject of residuals. “I look at that time and I was like, we paid them,” Song said. “I always say this about my time at Disney, is like, I know everybody has their own journey [because]… I always say, like, I have a boring tale… I had a lovely time.”
	

	Song did admit that she passed out on set once while filming a scene that called for a hot tub, which malfunctioned and was heated to “250 degrees,” said Sprouse. “I remember just breathing really heavy, and my chest felt really hot. I just went, ‘Am I having a panic attack?’ And then all of a sudden I remember stars and gone.”

	She continued: “I think the only thing that was hard about that time was I feel like we were underpaid and overworked. But Disney did give us a platform to be sitting here right now. So it’s very hard to complain about certain things.”

	Earlier this month, Sprouse also touched on how the show was “extremely underfunded,” despite being “popular” on his podcast. “In terms of the channel higher-ups, we were also kind of weirdly the ugly duckling,” Sprouse said, before adding that “the only residual check I’ve ever received for ‘The Suite Life’ at all was a crossover episode with ‘Hannah Montana’ for five cents. I’m not joking,” he said. “Imagine that. In a time where residuals would have been great,” Sprouse added, “Not a single paycheck for being arguably one of the most popular shows.”
	

	The “The Suite Life of Zack and Cody” ran from 2005 to 2008 and followed the titular Zack and Cody as they lived at the Tipton Hotel with their single mother. Song played teenage heiress London Tipton. The show inspired a spinoff, “The Suite Life on Deck,” which aired from 2008 to 2011. Song, Debby Ryan, Erin Cardillo and more starred in the continuation.

schema.headline: Brenda Song Says She Was ‘Overworked’ and ‘Underpaid’ on ‘The Suite Life of Zack and Cody,’ Recalls Fainting on Set: I Thought, ‘Am I Having a Panic Attack?’

title: Stacy Keach, Star of ‘Mike Hammer,’ ‘Fat City,’ Dies at 85
description: Stacy Keach, a commanding actor whose work includes movies like “Fat City” and the starring role in “The New Mike Hammer” series on CBS, died Tuesd
body:
Stacy Keach, a commanding actor whose work includes movies like “Fat City” and the starring role in “The New Mike Hammer” series on CBS, died Tuesday in Poland. He was 85.

	His wife, Małgosia Tomassi, confirmed his death to Variety. In a statement, she said he died “after a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure” at the family’s home in Magdalenka, Poland.


	“Stacy was not only a legendary actor, admired and loved by audiences the world over, but also my beloved husband, my companion and the heart of our family,” the statement said. “His passing leaves an immeasurable emptiness in our lives. But his extraordinary spirit, his unforgettable voice and the love he gave so generously will remain with us forever.
	

	Active on stage, film and TV into his eighties, he popped up in “The Bourne Legacy,” “Nebraska,” “Two and a Half Men,” “Ray Donovan” and had a recurring voice role on “The Simpsons.” Keach was also known for playing Cardinal Kevin Kearns on “Blue Bloods.” His TV appearances included “Man With a Plan” and “The Black List.” His final role was in “Jay Kelly” in 2025, as the father of Jay Kelly, played by George Clooney.

	In 2010, he received a Helen Hayes award for his performance of “King Lear,” for Shakespeare Theater Co., one of many stage honors over the course of his career.

	Keach got his Tony nomination for playing Buffalo Bill in the 1969 Broadway production “Indians” early on but garnered even more fame as “Mike Hammer.” The CBS series aired from 1984-87 and he reprised the role in the 1989 TV movie “Mike Hammer: Murder Takes All” and the syndicated series “Mike Hammer, Private Eye” in 1997-98. He also narrated the CNBC series, “American Greed.” 
	

	Keach’s run as the private detective got off to a rocky start off screen, however. In 1984, police arrested Keach at London’s Heathrow Airport for possession of cocaine. Pleading guilty, the actor served six months at Reading Prison. Since Keach also narrated “Mike Hammer” in character, impressionist Rich Little was called to sub in as the show’s narrator during Keach’s imprisonment.

	In a 2014 television interview, Keach declared that his time in prison was (understandably) the low point of his life, and a friendship he formed with a priest during that time led to his conversion to Roman Catholicism.

	Keach’s Emmy nomination came shortly after that period; he was recognized in 1988 for outstanding lead actor in a miniseries or special for playing the famous author of the title in “Ernest Hemingway.”

	Part of an acting family that includes his younger brother James, who has gone on to direct and produce, Walter Stacy Keach Jr. was born in Savannah, Ga., the son of actress Mary Cain and Stacy Keach Sr., an actor, drama teacher and theater director. Class president at Van Nuys High School, he graduated from UC Berkeley in 1963, and went on to earn a graduate degree at the Yale School of Drama. He was also a Fulbright Scholar at the London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art.

	In 1966, Keach played the title role in Barbara Garson’s Off Broadway anti-war satire “MacBird!,”winning his first Obie Award. The following year he appeared Off Broadway again, this time with Morgan Freeman (in the latter’s acting debut) in George Tabori’s provocatively titled “The Niggerlovers.”

	Keach made his Broadway debut in Georg Buchner’s “Danton’s Death” in 1965, soon thereafter appearing in a revival of “The Country Wife,” followed by the original Broadway production of Bertolt Brecht play “The Caucasian Chalk Circle” and a 1968 staging of “King Lear” in which he played Edmund. The following year he starred in Arthur Kopit’s “Indians,” picking up his Tony nomination for his performance as Buffalo Bill.

	He returned to Broadway in 1979 as a replacement for John Wood as Sidney Bruhl in Ira Levin’s long-running mystery comedy “Deathtrap,” starred in “Solitary Confinement” in 1992 and in Robert Schenkkan’s “The Kentucky Cycle” the following year.

	Off Broadway, Keach appeared twice in “Hamlet,” in 1964 and 1972, the second time in the title role, winning his second Obie. He also appeared as Falstaff in Henry “IV” Parts I and II in 1968, and as James Tyrone Jr. in O’Neill’s “Long Day’s Journey Into Night” in 1971.
	

	In the early 1980s he starred in the title role of the national touring company of the Cy Coleman musical “Barnum.” He performed the title role in “King Lear” at the Goodman Theater in 2006, and in 2008 played Merlin in a semi-staged version of “Camelot” with the New York Philharmonic.

	Keach played Richard M. Nixon in the U.S. traveling version of the play “Frost/Nixon” in 2008 and 2009, in the course of which — one day in March 2009 — he had a series of strokes, from he recovered sufficiently to take another go at “King Lear” in D.C. that summer.

	Keach was a founding member of L.A. Theatre Works.

	The actor debuted on TV in an episode of college drama “Channing” in 1964, followed by a TV movie versions of Shakespeare’s “The Winter’s Tale” (1967), in which he played Autolycus, and “Macbeth” (1968), in which he played Banquo. Also in 1968 the actor made his big-screen debut in the adaptation of Carson McCullers’ “The Heart Is a Lonely Hunter.”

	He played a crippled millionaire in Robert Altman’s “Brewster McCloud” (1970) and by the next year he starred in the title role of the Western “Doc,” playing Doc Holliday opposite Faye Dunaway.

	In John Huston’s boxing drama “Fat City” (1972), Keach was the over-the-hill boxer praying for a comeback, and Jeff Bridges was the young boxer on the rise.

	Also in 1972 the actor starred with George C. Scott and Jane Alexander in the adaptation of Joseph Wambaugh’s “The New Centurions” and had a supporting role in Huston’s “The Life and Times of Judge Roy Bean.” He played in a number of roles before stoner comedy classic “Up in Smoke” (1978).

	“The Ninth Configuration” (1980), directed by Willliam Peter Blatty and adapted by him from his own surrealist novel “Twinkle Twinkle ‘Killer’ Kane,” became a cult favorite, with Keach’s as Marine Col. Vincent Kane who runs a hospital for military men with psychiatric problems.

	Also in 1980, the actor appeared with his brother James Keach as Frank and Jesse James in “The Long Riders,” and in 1982 he starred with Bruce Dern, Robert Mitchum, Martin Sheen and Paul Sorvino in Jason Miller’s “That Championship Season.”

	Additional film credits include Oliver Stone’s biopic “W.” (2008), John Sayles’ “Honeydripper” (2007) and “Sin City: A Dame to Kill For” (2014). He had a recurring role on “ER” and the Fox comedy “Titus.”
	

	H has made numerous guest appearances on shows including “Touched by an Angel,” “Will & Grace,” “George Lopez,” “30 Rock” (as himself), “Anger Management,” “Brooklyn Nine-Nine,” “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit,” “NCIS: New Orleans” and “Hot in Cleveland.”

	Keach was married four times, first to Kathryn Baker in 1964, then to Marilyn Aiken from 1975-79 and to Jill Donahue from 1981-86.

	He is survived by fourth wife Malgosia Tomassi, whom he married in 1986; son Shannon and daughter Karolina and his brother James Keach.

schema.headline: Stacy Keach, Star of ‘Mike Hammer,’ ‘Fat City,’ Dies at 85

title: Norwegian Oscar Entry ‘Growth of the Soil’ Sells to North America, U.K., Germany, Spain and More
description: Beta Cinema has closed a raft of major deals on Hans Petter Moland’s epic love story “Growth of the Soil,” Norway’s entry for best international fe
body:
Beta Cinema has closed a raft of major deals on Hans Petter Moland’s epic love story “Growth of the Soil,” Norway’s entry for best international feature film at the 99th Academy Awards. The deals follow the film’s world premiere in Toronto and its European premiere at San Sebastián, where it walked away with two major awards.

	The film has sold to Greenwich Entertainment in North America, Neue Visionen in Germany and Austria, Teodora Film in Italy, A Contracorriente Films in Spain, Conic in the U.K. and Ireland, Cherry Pickers in Benelux, Frenetic Films in Switzerland, Weird Wave in Greece, Scanorama in the Baltics, Vertigo Media in Hungary, Beta Film in Bulgaria, Big Tree Entertainment in India, Falcon Pictures in Indonesia, Imovision in Brazil and Palace Films in Australia and New Zealand.
	

	The film was released throughout Scandinavia by Scanbox Entertainment, and got off to a strong start in Norway, climbing to No. 1 at the box office over its opening weekend.

	At San Sebastián, “Growth of the Soil” won the Silver Shell for best leading performance and the jury prize for best cinematography. The film has subsequently continued its autumn festival run, including showings at the Warsaw Film Festival, the Rio Film Festival, the Denver Film Festival, the Mar del Plata Film Festival and it opened the Bergen Film Festival. It also is shortlisted for the European Film Awards for the best feature film category.

	Based on a Nobel Prize Winning novel, “Growth of the Soil” tells the story of Isak, a man without a past who crosses the mountains in search of somewhere to build a life. High above the tree line, he finds an unforgiving stretch of land and, eventually, Inger, a woman whose resilience matches his own. Together they create a home and family from almost nothing, until time, ambition and a changing world begin to transform both their relationship and the landscape around them.
	

	Herbert Nordrum (“The Worst Person in the World,” “Sense and Sensibility”) and former EFP Shooting Star Asta Kamma August (“The Hypnosis”) are in the leading roles, next to Gard B. Eidsvold, Anders Baasmo, Oddgeir Thune and Sjur Vatne Brean.

	Moland previously directed “Out Stealing Horses,” “In Order of Disappearance,” “A Somewhat Gentle Man” and “Zero Kelvin.” His films have competed for the Golden Bear four times, and “Out Stealing Horses” was Norway’s Oscar submission in 2019.

	Moland co-wrote the screenplay with Eidsvold. The film was shot by Oskar Dahlsbakken, with an original score by Danish composer Kaspar Kaae. It is produced by Håkon Øverås for 4 ½ Fiction, in co-production with Scanbox.

schema.headline: Norwegian Oscar Entry ‘Growth of the Soil’ Sells to North America, U.K., Germany, Spain and More

title: Bay Theater in Pacific Palisades Reopens Friday With ‘Ebenezer’
description: The Bay Theater in Pacific Palisades will officially reopen on Friday, a month after it was announced that Paramount Pictures is taking over the ci
body:
The Bay Theater in Pacific Palisades will officially reopen on Friday, a month after it was announced that Paramount Pictures is taking over the cinemas. 

	Paramount Pictures, Caruso and The Lot have reimagined the theaters with cutting-edge cinema technology that includes “luxury seating, elevated dining and exceptional hospitality, while preserving the intimate neighborhood character that has made it a community favorite.”


	Previously operated by Netflix, the theaters have been closed since the devastating wildfires in January 2025. The multiplex is located in Rick Caruso’s Palisades Village shopping area, which reopened in August after extensive remediation and repairs due to the fires. 
	

	First-run films playing at the Bay include Johnny Depp’s “Ebenezer,” which opens nationwide Friday, as well as “The Cat in the Hat,” “Wild Horse Nine,” “You Can See Everything” and “Godzilla Minus Zero.”

	Operated by luxury dine-in cinema company The Lot, the Bay offers five auditoriums with immersive surround sound and laser projection. Theaters include customizable seating with adjustable foot, back, head and neck rests, USB charging, personal dining tables with custom lighting and service buttons for food and beverage ordering.

	The made-to-order menu, served directly to seats, includes appetizers, snacks, burgers, entrées and desserts, plus a premium beverage program with wine, beer, mocktails and signature cocktails including the Pacific Blush, Sunset Mule and Coastline Cantarito.

	The lounge area and full-service bar feature a video wall for sports viewing, giving moviegoers a place to gather before and after films.
	

	In addition to first-run films, the Bay will program nostalgic classics, curated screenings and special events.

schema.headline: Bay Theater in Pacific Palisades Reopens Friday With ‘Ebenezer’

title: Elliot Frances Flynn and Michael Paré to Star in Indie Supernatural Horror ‘Not Herself’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Elliot Frances Flynn (“Peacemaker“) will star alongside Michael Paré (“Streets of Fire”) in Jon Russell Cring and Tracy Nichole Cring’s supernatura
body:
Elliot Frances Flynn (“Peacemaker“) will star alongside Michael Paré (“Streets of Fire”) in Jon Russell Cring and Tracy Nichole Cring’s supernatural horror film “Not Herself,” which recently wrapped production in New York.

	The Crings co-wrote and co-directed “Not Herself,” which, according to an official description, “centers on Izmarie (Flynn), a guilt-ridden young woman haunted by a tragic accident in her past. Seeking a fresh start, she moves into a sprawling old house and begins offering psychic readings, exposing the secrets of those around her. But as her visions become increasingly prophetic and menacing, Izmarie begins to suspect something inside the house is speaking through her.” Paré co-stars as Reverend Charles Weathers, “a threatening presence in Izmarie’s new life.”
	

	Flynn recently appeared in Season 2 of HBO’s “Peacemaker.” Her other recent TV credits include “Long Bright River” and “Only Murders in the Building.” On the big screen, she’s appeared in “Shoplifters of the World,” “Linoleum,” “Unidentified Objects” and “Confession.” Flynn’s upcoming work includes the rom-com “Silent Retreat,” starring Isabella Rossellini.

	Paré broke into Hollywood starring in “Eddie and the Cruisers” and “Streets of Fire,” both mid-’80s cult classics. His other big-screen credits include “Village of the Damned,” “Bad Moon,” “The Virgin Suicides,” “Bone Tomahawk” and “Puppet Master: The Littlest Reich.”

	Jon Russell Cring and Tracy Nichole Cring are a husband-and-wife filmmaking duo that has produced 20 feature films together. Their other film releases include “Wheelies Inc.,” “Girl in the Palms” and “Darcy.” Their most recent project, “Sky Valley,” starring Morningstar Angeline, Irene Bedard and DJ Qualls, wrapped production in 2025.

schema.headline: Elliot Frances Flynn and Michael Paré to Star in Indie Supernatural Horror ‘Not Herself’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Is ‘I Play Rocky’ Original or Adapted? Stallone’s ‘Rocky’ Origin Story Faces a ‘Barbie’-Style Oscar Dilemma (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Sylvester Stallone wrote “Rocky” in three days. Figuring out which Oscar screenplay category the movie about him writing it belongs in is taking a
body:
Sylvester Stallone wrote “Rocky” in three days. Figuring out which Oscar screenplay category the movie about him writing it belongs in is taking a lot longer.

	Amazon MGM Studios’ “I Play Rocky” has been the subject of multiple conversations among the studio, the Writers Guild of America, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and the film’s creative team over whether Peter Gamble’s script will compete as an original or adapted screenplay. No determination has been made.
	

	Thursday, Nov. 12, is the final deadline for studios to submit Official Screen Credits (OSC) forms to the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences for the 99th Academy Awards in the best picture, animated feature and general entry categories. No films afterward will be considered.

	Gamble conceived and wrote the script as an original, and it isn’t based on a book, article, memoir or any other single published work. He drafted it on spec, and Bellevue Productions, shared it with Christian Baha of Baha Films. Baha came aboard as a producer alongside Toby Emmerich, and director Peter Farrelly, who helmed best picture winner “Green Book” (2018), eventually signed on. It’s Gamble’s second produced feature script after “Office Uprising” (2018).

	But “Rocky” is one of the most established pieces of IP in Hollywood, and sources say some within each organization are weighing whether the screenplay is a better fit for adapted, the category for scripts built on previously established material. Rocky Balboa, Adrian and Apollo Creed are preexisting characters and Farrelly’s film restages some of the 1976 movie’s best-known scenes, written half a century ago.
	

	Amazon MGM and the Academy declined to comment.

	“I Play Rocky” expands nationwide Nov. 20, the same day WGA submissions close, but the guild won’t be weighing in. The film wasn’t produced under a WGA signatory agreement, so the guild can’t classify the screenplay or consider it for the WGA Awards, even though Gamble is a member. That leaves the decision entirely to the Academy’s Writers Branch executive committee, which makes its own determinations and has broken with the WGA before.

	Elsewhere on the circuit, the question will carry less weight. The Golden Globes put all screenplays in a single category, while BAFTA and the Critics Choice Awards, which split original and adapted, generally go with the category the studio submits.

	According to the Academy’s screenplay submission FAQ for the 99th Oscars, films don’t submit to a specific writing category. Instead, the Writers Branch executive committee reviews each eligible title and generally defers to the WGA’s classification, except when the guild hasn’t classified a film, as is the case with “I Play Rocky” or its classification “has been called into question.” The guidelines cut both ways for Gamble’s script. 

	A script is generally deemed adapted if it’s based on a sequel, a remake, an existing film or “pre-existing characters,” but it’s considered original if it tells a true story in which the writer “performed their own research and used multiple sources.” While a determination is under review, the committee may ask the film’s credited writers for a statement. Once it rules, the decision is final and no appeals or additional materials are accepted.

	We seem to have one of these every awards season.

	In January 2024, Greta Gerwig’s “Barbie” was moved to adapted after Warner Bros. campaigned it as an original and the WGA classified as well. Barbie and Ken existed as Mattel dolls long before Gerwig and Noah Baumbach turned them into a billion-dollar sensation, and there were multiple cartoons that existed with the characters. Ultimately, the script earned an adapted nomination and lost to Cord Jefferson’s “American Fiction.”

	Category reversals aren’t new. Barry Jenkins’ “Moonlight,” Damien Chazelle’s “Whiplash” and Joel and Ethan Coen’s “The Ballad of Buster Scruggs” all carried original labels from the WGA before the Academy shifted them to adapted. The Academy has also long treated sequels as adaptations because their characters come from earlier films, which is how “Before Sunset,” “Toy Story 3,” “Top Gun: Maverick” and “Glass Onion” all landed in adapted.
	

	That rule is being tested again this season. Aaron Sorkin’s “The Social Reckoning,” which dramatizes whistleblower Frances Haugen’s 2021 Facebook leak and Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz’s coverage of it, was initially marketed as a sequel to “The Social Network” (2010), which won Sorkin the adapted screenplay Oscar. The WGA has classified the new film as an original. There’s no word yet on whether the Academy’s committee will accept that designation.



	

					(L to R) Stephan James as Carl Weathers and Anthony Ippolito as Sylvester Stallone in I PLAY ROCKY, from Amazon MGM Studios.
									Claire Folger
	



	That’s the precedent Gamble’s script has to get around, and there’s a strong counterargument. “I Play Rocky” isn’t a sequel, a prequel or a spinoff. It’s a biographical drama about a real person, and biopics have routinely competed as originals. Dustin Lance Black won original screenplay for “Milk,” even though Harvey Milk’s life had already been chronicled in the Oscar-winning documentary “The Times of Harvey Milk.” Anthony McCarten’s “Darkest Hour” also competed as an original, despite covering Winston Churchill’s first weeks as prime minister, a chapter that fills every high school history textbook.

	Movies about the making of movies are interesting territory, and they have produced originals, too. “Saving Mr. Banks,” about the making of “Mary Poppins,” competed as an original but didn’t land a nomination. Neither did Jason Reitman and Gil Kenan’s “Saturday Night,” which follows the 90 minutes leading up to the first televised episode of “Saturday Night Live.” Netflix’s “Mank,” written by the late Jack Fincher, father of director David Fincher, chronicles screenwriter Herman J. Mankiewicz’s work on Orson Welles’ “Citizen Kane” (1941). It was also deemed an original, and it also missed in the category, even as the film led the field with 10 nominations.

	When a making-of film does land in adapted, there’s usually a book behind it. Scott Neustadter and Michael H. Weber’s “The Disaster Artist,” for example, was based on Greg Sestero and Tom Bissell’s 2013 nonfiction book of the same name. A public figure’s life, however, is fair game, as illustrated by A24’s Chris Hansen story, “Primetime,” which Ajon Singh based on an article by Luke Dittrich. 
	

	Interestingly, Amazon MGM owns the “Rocky” franchise. The 1976 original earned 10 Oscar nominations and won best picture, and Stallone was nominated for best actor and original screenplay. Director Farrelly knows the original side all too well, as he shared the original screenplay Oscar with Brian Hayes Currie and Nick Vallelonga for “Green Book,” another true story that drew from no single published source.

	Where the film lands could reshape its trajectory, and both races are stacked. In original, Jesse Eisenberg (“The Debut”), Jordan Firstman (“Club Kid”), Mike Leigh (“Tender Loving Care”), Martin McDonagh (“Wild Horse Nine”) and Simon Rich (“Artificial”) are all in the conversation. A move to adapted wouldn’t clear the road. It would put Gamble up against Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” Drew Goddard’s “Project Hail Mary” and Rashida Jones and Will McCormack’s “The Invite,” along with Los Javis’ “La Bola Negra” and Denis Villeneuve’s yet-to-be-screened “Dune: Part Three.”

	“I Play Rocky” has been gaining momentum since its world premiere at TIFF. It finished first runner-up for the People’s Choice Award behind “La Bola Negra” and was the runner-up at Middleburg. It was also the audience choice winner at Cinéfest Sudbury International Film Festival, and recently Ippolito was honored with the breakthrough award at SCAD Savannah Film Festival. It recently opened on Nov. 6 in seven theaters, capturing $345,000 from seven theaters, averaging $49,200 per location. The film has also made one category call already: it’s submitted at the Golden Globes as a musical or comedy, joining a field that includes “Wild Horse Nine,” “The Debut” and Amazon MGM stablemate “Project Hail Mary.”

	The Academy’s final word likely won’t surface until nominations voting opens Jan. 11, 2027. Before that, the WGA announces its screenplay nominees Jan. 8. Oscar nominations will be announced Jan. 21, and the 99th Oscars take place March 14.

schema.headline: Is ‘I Play Rocky’ Original or Adapted? Stallone’s ‘Rocky’ Origin Story Faces a ‘Barbie’-Style Oscar Dilemma (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Jinkx Monsoon and BenDeLaCreme on Taking Their Holiday Show on the Road and Paying Tribute to ‘Queer Icons’ Tim Curry and Dolly Parton
description: Yes, there are the Rockettes at Radio City Music Hall, but actors, writers, comedians and drag queens Jinkx Monsoon and BenDelaCreme are back to sl
body:
Yes, there are the Rockettes at Radio City Music Hall, but actors, writers, comedians and drag queens Jinkx Monsoon and BenDelaCreme are back to slay with one of the greatest and funniest winter shows — The Jinkx and Dela Holiday Show! This year, Monsoon and Dela celebrate their ninth year of taking the show on the road, and with last week’s blue tsunami, there’s plenty of festive cheer to go around as both are feeling a renewed sense of holiday spirit.
	

	“It is a nice contrast to when we did this show two years ago. We had our first preview the night that [Trump] won for a second time, and it felt hard to get on stage then because we knew that there was a lot of BS in store. It’s been a very sordid time to be a queer and trans person,” Monsoon says as the pair get ready to play at The Eastern Theater in Atlanta, Ga.

	This year, the tour will take them around the country to Cincinnati, New York, Cleveland, Detroit and San Francisco. And as is tradition, the show will play in Seattle from Dec. 21 through Dec. 24 — the city where their friendship first began. Tickets are already in high demand.

	Here the pair spoke with Variety about the new show and the secret to their collaboration.
	
		How does it feel to be taking this show on the road and being in Atlanta amid this blue tsunami?	

	JINKX MONSOON: I have been continually bolstered and fortified by the fact that when we take this show around the country, and we pack our houses, things might be the way they are, but I know there’s a room full of people who feel and think the same way that I do — and that’s everywhere. Our community exists everywhere. The queer community is a global community, and it’s wonderful to remember that. Even at the darkest times, we have a community to turn to. I can’t take any responsibility, but it feels like a Christmas miracle to not have to be fighting as hard to get people to listen to something that should be basic information.
	

	BENDELACRÈME: Every year, we try to create a show that speaks to where we’re at collectively. But this year’s show is about how the future is always unknown. It’s always scary, and it’s always true that nothing is inevitable. We’ve been fed a lot of rhetoric about inevitable futures, and the next thing can be anything. And so, to write a show with that content and then get to open it riding this wave of hope — but also remembering that the conversations don’t happen by themselves — is very special. We’ve got to keep up with it. We’ve got to stay behind it. It’s very exciting — things coinciding in a way that’s just celebratory and hopeful.
	
		I love the theme that a billionaire, aka Ebenezer Scrooge, buys out the holiday show. How did you come up with that theme, and how did Ebenezer become a part of it?	

	MONSOON: We like to have the serious conversations in the stupidest way possible. With the Christmas/Winter holiday lens, we try to keep it in the world of commonly recognizable fictional Christmas characters, and luckily, there’s a large repertoire to pull from. Scrooge really fits the build this year.

	What I love about the show is that we’re having conversations that every artist out there is having: How do I make a living being an artist while staying true to creating art? I also have to feed myself, and this all doesn’t just happen magically for free. It’s the dilemma a lot of artists are facing. Do you want to be an artist or do you want to eat? And for a long time, you haven’t had to decide one or the other. But art has been attacked and left out to fend for itself recently, and everything’s about what’s going to make money, not what’s the best possible art. So I think, as a performer, I’m very excited to be a live entertainer because, for whatever reason, art is surviving and thriving in live entertainment — even though a lot of filmed media feels like it’s being pushed through the same sausage maker of capitalism.

	DELA: Fortunately, for now, live entertainment — seeing a performer in front of you — is one of the few things we can still really trust is real and happening, right? It’s very scary, but I think we’re also all really learning to be skeptical in a way that’s really important. It’s also really hard to approach everything with a sense of, “Can I believe this?” But when you’re in a room with someone, you know it’s real. It’s in front of your eyes, but you can also feel it, right? You don’t exchange energy with people over a screen in the same way. You don’t. People can feel each other’s presence, and they can feel what it means. I think that’s part of why live performance continues to thrive and will continue to thrive.
	
	
		The show has a tribute to Tim Curry and Dolly Parton. How did you weave those icons in?	

	MONSOON: Every year we come to our first writing session like a completely blank slate. Usually, Dela has a couple of assignments — maybe there’s a top 40 song, or there’s a cultural moment or there was a movie — and she says, “We are doing a disservice to our audience if we don’t get a bit in about this thing.” This year, we lost two huge multigenerational queer icons who are very much alive in the zeitgeist and still are.

	Dela just came to the table saying, “I don’t know how we’re going to do it, but we got to get a Dolly song, and we got to get a Tim Curry song, and I think I know which Tim Curry song. We’ve just got to find the right way.” And the way she found to incorporate it is so perfectly suited to the taste of “The Jinkx and Dela Holiday Show.” It’s so perfect. It’s nothing you would have imagined outside of the context of “The Jinkx and Dela Holiday Show,” but within the show, it’s a seat of honor.

	This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

schema.headline: Jinkx Monsoon and BenDeLaCreme on Taking Their Holiday Show on the Road and Paying Tribute to ‘Queer Icons’ Tim Curry and Dolly Parton

title: ‘Risa and the Wind Phone’ Wins Audience Award at Miami Film Festival Gems – Film News in Brief
description:
“Risa and the Wind Phone” is the winner of the Miami Film Festival Gems 2026 Audience Award

	Directed by Juan Cabral, the film follows Risa, who d
body:
“Risa and the Wind Phone” is the winner of the Miami Film Festival Gems 2026 Audience Award

	Directed by Juan Cabral, the film follows Risa, who discovers she has the ability to communicate with her deceased father from beyond the grave. As she explores this supernatural connection, she faces emotional challenges and family secrets that will test her faith in what she thought was possible.


	“Elsinore” was the first runner-up. From director Simon Stone and writer Stephen Beresford, the film tells the true story of actor Ian Charleson (Andrew Scott) stepping into the role of Hamlet at London’s National Theatre while privately battling AIDS, in a performance that became the triumph of his career.
	

	The second runner-up was “I Play Rocky” directed by Peter Farrelly. It’s the based on a true story account of the unknown actor who believed he wasn’t meant to just write “Rocky,” but to play Rocky Balboa.
	
		Tuesday, Nov. 10	

	Amblin Entertainment CEO Jeff Small Elected to Ronald McDonald House Board of TrusteesCEO of Amblin Entertainment Jeff Small has been elected to the board of trustees of Ronald McDonald House Westside Los Angeles.

	Ronald McDonald House Westside Los Angeles is currently engaged in a $50 million capital campaign to support the acquisition and transformation of a former boutique hotel in Westwood Village into a four-story Ronald McDonald House.

	The organization aims to provide essential services that remove barriers, strengthen families and promote healing when children need healthcare.

	Small currently serves on the board of directors of both the Weingart Center, a comprehensive human services organization serving unhoused men and women in L.A., and Starlight Children’s Foundation, a nonprofit organization dedicated to improving the emotional and social well-being of hospitalized children. He has also served on multiple committees benefiting the USC Shoah Foundation and the USC Keck School of Medicine and continues to serve on several advisory and leadership committees for Stanford University.
	
	
		Monday Nov. 9	

	‘De Gaulle,’ ‘La Gradiva’ and ‘Alice: Pioneer Of Cinema’ Among American French Film Fest Winners

	The American French Film Festival announced the winners of this year’s awards during the closing ceremony on Nov. 8.

	The films were voted on by audiences attending the festival, members of the Los Angeles Film Critics Association, a jury of entertainment professionals and a student jury consisting of high school and college-age participants from the TAFFF High School Screenings Program.

	“De Gaulle,” written by Antonin Baudry and Bérénice Vila, directed by Antonin Baudry and Niels Schneider, Benoît Magimel and Anamaria Vartolomei, took home the Audience Award and top honor for best film.

	The Critics Award for best film was given to “La Gradiva.” Written by Marine Atlan and Anne Brouillet, the film is directed by Marine Atlan and stars Colas Quignard, Antonia Buresi, Mitia Capellier-Audat and Suzanne Gerin.

	“A Place For Her” received the First Feature Award; “Whispers In The Woods” received the Documentary Film Award; “The Green Eyes” received American Students Award; “Alice: Pioneer Of Cinema” received the Audience Series Award; “Swapped” received the Jury Series Award; “Diego” received the Audience Short Film Award; “God is Shy” received the Jury Short Film Award.

	Diversity and Inclusion Film Festival Set for N.Y.’s Lincoln Center

	The Distribution Collective will host the annual Diversity and Inclusion Film Festival at the Lincoln Center campus from Nov. 13 to Nov. 15.

	Special programming will include a Universal Studio Group panel on Nov. 14, featuring Hanako Greensmith (“Chicago Fire”), Zeeko Zaki (“FBI”) and David Ajala (“Law & Order”), who will discuss carrying forward the legacy of Wolf Entertainment’s iconic television franchises while introducing new dimensions to beloved series. 

	“DIFF was founded on the belief that storytelling has the power to bring communities together, challenge perceptions and create lasting opportunities for artists whose voices deserve to be heard,” said Sola Fasehun, the festival’s founder. “Our continued film festival at Lincoln Center in New York reflects that commitment in action. For several years, we’ve had the opportunity to introduce New York audiences to an incredible range of filmmakers through our programming, and we’re thrilled to be back at Lincoln Center for another year of welcoming filmmakers and supporting film and TV.”

title: Turning Point USA Denies Involvement in Alleged Rutgers University Assault
description:
Turning Point USA
                          Fires Back at Student Assault Allegation
body:
Turning Point USA
                          Fires Back at Student Assault Allegation
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              November 10, 2026
                            7:25 PM PST
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  November 10, 2026
                                7:57 PM PST
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A woman who claims to be a former volunteer Rutgers University student chapter Vice President of Turning Point USA says she was assaulted at one of their events in Maryland, however Turning Point denies their employees knew of the situation or were involved ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            The woman said in video shared to social media that earlier this year she attended a social event where several male members had "assaulted and violated" her. She reported the incidence to local police, but there is no word on the status of their investigation.
      
    
            A Turning Point legal representative tells TMZ ... the organization "takes assault allegations incredibly seriously" and they have a rigorous response process.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The rep continues ... "When we were notified of the incident in October, more than 3 months after the July event in question, we immediately launched an internal investigation and attempted to interview all those involved. While multiple people in the room or with knowledge of the incident provided statements, videos, and text messages, [accusers name] declined to participate on four different occasions."
      

            We're told by the organization ... "The room in which the alleged incident occurred was not part of the Turning Point USA room block" and that "individuals independently booked that room."
      
    
            The organization tells us everyone who was interviewed "were adamant that no sexual assault occurred." Turning Point tells TMZ the blood on [her] clothing was from her period, not a result of any assault, according to people who were there.
      
    
            The rep says "The Rutgers PD report that was eventually filed on October 26th also doesn't include any allegations of sexual assault, but instead references video 'that appears to depict consensual face-slapping with [the accuser] slapping an unidentified male and pillow fighting.'"
      
    
            The organization tells TMZ ... "The male student involved in the alleged incident was removed from the event the next day following an unrelated matter, after which he was immediately disinvited from future events and has no affiliation with the organization."
      
    
            The rep is adamant "At no point were any TPUSA staff involved, nor was staff made aware of these allegations during the event. Had they been brought to our attention, we would have immediately assisted the student in engaging law enforcement and provided all necessary support. Student safety remains our top priority."

body:
Ole Miss Racist Video
                          Girls Claimed They Were 'Stimming' When They Made Monkey Noises

                              November 10, 2026
                            4:45 PM PST
                                                                      |

                                  November 10, 2026
                                6:04 PM PST
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A roommate of the Ole Miss student who released video of fellow students making monkey noises at their ring camera says the girls claimed to be "stimming" during the offensive behavior.
      
    
            Bethany Joyy re-shared the viral video on Facebook, claiming the girls later apologized ... but also asked if the video was going to be deleted.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            She wrote that she could hear the girls making the monkey noises from inside and confronted them when they saw the video from the ring camera.
      

            Bethany wrote ... "Once we saw the footage, we came outside and asked them if they did it, told them it was disrespectful etc."
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            She continued ... "While we were doing this, the monkey sounds continued. We returned inside. My roommate came into contact with them again and was brushed off."
      
    
            According to Bethany, it was only after the video was uploaded that the girls apologized, claiming to be "stimming" and making animal noises in other people's ring cameras, too.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            She wrote ... "As u can see in the video, there is another ring camera across the hall that remained untouched. After they apologized, one of the first things that was asked was about if the video was going to be deleted or not."
      
    
            Bethany said this is the first time the girls have exhibited this kind of behavior toward them, adding ... "We have had conversations with them before and none of them were hostile or anything. My friends and I are extremely polite to anyone who comes near our apartment and all of our neighbors can attest to that."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As we previously reported, Alaina Kunes -- one of the girls who made monkey noises -- voluntarily withdrew from Ole Miss after the video went viral.
      
    
            Her family's business is also facing a lawsuit over alleged racism by its employees at their business.
